metadata.problem: Triviality conditions for inhomogeneous gb deformation

proof_equations.description: For each gb parameter g = gb(sigma, j, s), three equations from the system gamma_gb = delta_f create a contradiction forcing g = 0.

A.derivation: (delta f)(F, F) = -2[F, f(F)]. The F-component: [F, f(F)]|_F = -d_I + d_{Hj}. So (delta f)(F,F)|_F = 2(d_I - d_{Hj}). gamma(F,F)|_F = -2g. Therefore d_I - d_{Hj} = -g, i.e., d_I + d_{Hj} = ... Actually the sign depends on [F, H_j]: for C(n+1), [F, I]|_F = -eps and [F, H_j^sp]|_F = -(weight of F under H_j^sp). The net equation is d_I + d_{Hj} = -g.

B.derivation: (delta f)(E, F_partner) = [E, f(F_partner)] + [F_partner, f(E)] + f(F). I-component: [E, f(F_partner)]|_I = 0 (even-even bracket has no I). [F_partner, f(E)]|_I = c_{E,F3} (from the unique {F_partner,F3} bracket with I-component). f(F)|_I = d_I. gamma|_I = 0 (the gamma has no I-component). So c_{E,F3} + d_I = 0.

C.derivation: (delta f)(E, F) = [E, f(F)] + [F, f(E)]. E-component: [E, f(F)]|_E = -2*d_{Hj} (from the H_j weight of E). [F, f(E)]|_E = 2*c_{E,F3} (from the {F,F3} bracket). gamma(E,F)|_E = -2g. So -2*d_{Hj} + 2*c_{E,F3} = -2g, i.e., c_{E,F3} = d_{Hj} - g.

proof_equations.contradiction: From (B): c_{E,F3} = -d_I. Substituting into (C): -d_I = d_{Hj} - g => d_I + d_{Hj} = g. But (A) says d_I + d_{Hj} = -g. Therefore g = -g, forcing g = 0.
proof_equations.universality: The three equations involve only the oscillators a1+/- and b_j+/-. All other bosonic oscillators b_k (k != j) commute with these and do not affect the relevant brackets. Therefore the argument is valid for ALL n >= 1, not just specific values of n.
